title: NIS2 Directive — AI System Classification Under Essential and Important Entity Rules (Enforcement 2026)
context: 2026-08-29 engine cycle — answer-first seed mapping NIS2 entity classification to AI system obligations; aligned to Council of AI measurement posture
body: The NIS2 Directive (EU 2022/2555) expands cybersecurity obligations beyond critical infrastructure to cover essential and important entities across 18 sectors. As of the October 2024 transposition deadline, Member States were required to adopt national legislation; enforcement is now active across the EU throughout 2026. For AI system operators, the key question is: when does operating an AI system make you an essential or important entity, and what follows? The classification is sector-based, not technology-based. If your organisation falls into Annex I (essential: energy, transport, banking, financial market infrastructure, health, drinking water, digital infrastructure, ICT service management, public administration, space) or Annex II (important: postal, waste, chemicals, food, manufacturing of critical products, digital providers including online marketplaces and search engines, research), and meets the size thresholds (250+ employees / €50M+ turnover for essential; 50+ employees / €10M+ for important), you are in scope. AI systems deployed by these entities become part of the network and information systems subject to: (1) risk management measures proportionate to the risk (Art 21) — including incident handling, business continuity, supply chain security, and system acquisition security; (2) incident reporting obligations (Art 23) — significant incidents must be reported to the CSIRT within 24 hours (early warning), 72 hours (full notification), and one month (final report); (3) management body accountability — board members can be held personally liable for non-compliance and temporarily barred from management roles. For AI specifically, the intersection is in supply chain security: if your AI model, training pipeline, or inference endpoint is part of a critical service, the NIS2 risk management duty covers model provenance, data pipeline integrity, and inference-boundary monitoring. The Council of AI containment posture — monitored containment with signed measurement records — provides the audit trail NIS2 incident reporting demands: a detected containment breach is a reportable incident; a signed measurement index is the evidence. Practical 2026 timeline: national transpositions are live; competent authorities are issuing first enforcement guidance; the first wave of incident reports from AI-adjacent systems is expected in H2 2026 as mandatory reporting windows close.
